extracted.intended_audience: federal contracting officers, government procurement attorneys, and bidders/suppliers participating in U.S. Government procurement
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and legal standards governing solicitation, responsiveness, rejection, advertising, emergencies, and special exceptions in U.S. federal government contracting and bid evaluation. Covers when bids may be rejected, what constitutes material variance, advertising/competition requirements (section 3709 and related statutes), and exceptions (exigency, useless competition, open-market purchases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Related/affiliate bids do not alone justify rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if two bids are really submitted on behalf of the same company (e.g., a director submitted two very low bids and indicated company would manufacture if awarded), those facts alone do not constitute a fraud on the United States and do not justify rejection of the bids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere appearance of related submissions or low pricing by related bidders is insufficient to void bids; there must be fraud or other legally sufficient grounds to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for prior failure to fill contracts (G.O. 167 §3)
rubrics_metrics.description: "All bids received from contractors who have failed unjustifiably to fill former contracts with the Government shall be rejected."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is subject to case-by-case interpretation: isolated instances (e.g., misunderstanding of proposal, late delivery of shingles/lumber) may not constitute having "failed unjustifiably." An attempt to deliver inferior goods may be questionable as to whether it is an unjustifiable failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in more than one bid construed as bidder-interest (not manufacturer/seller)
rubrics_metrics.description: A clause providing that "reasonable grounds for supposing that any bidder is interested in more than one bid will be cause for rejection" refers to an interest as a bidder, not interest as a manufacturer or seller to a bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A manufacturer who quoted prices to a bidder is not thereby disqualified from submitting a direct bid for the same article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executed contract cannot be cancelled due to prior failures of contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after a contract has been duly subscribed and entered into with the lowest bidder, it is ascertained that the bidder had previously failed to perform another contract, that fact cannot authorize the Secretary of War to cancel the executed contract and enter into a new one with another party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized contracts are protected against unilateral cancellation on this ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidders not entitled to other bidders' prices from the Department
rubrics_metrics.description: A bidder is not entitled to be furnished by the War Department or its officers with the prices of other bidders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being present at bid opening and making memoranda is adequate; government personnel should not be used to furnish desired prices. Copies of bids may be obtained from the Interior Department returns office under statutory provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variance in place/time/quantity is material — bid nonresponsive
rubrics_metrics.description: A bid offering to furnish supplies or render services at a different place, at a time materially different (example: five months later), or in different quantity from that stated in the advertisement is a material variance and such a bid should not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letting a contract on such a bid would effectively make a contract without advertising. Examples: supplying lumber at Manila instead of specified Pacific coast port; bidding for a concrete tower when invite was for a steel tower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid terms on submitted documents control interpretation (conflicting specs)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a bid purports to be "subject to all the conditions and requirements" of the advertisement but adds specific design terms (e.g., reference to a blueprint specifying footings thirteen feet square while advertisement called for twenty feet), the bid should be construed according to the added specific design (i.e., thirteen feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typed or attached specific design terms on the bid form can narrow the bid to those specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government reservation to accept/reject any or part — partial acceptance issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the advertisement reserves the right to "reject or accept any or all proposals or any part thereof" and instructions state "time of deliveries will be considered," acceptance may be for part only; but whether such a partial award is responsive to the bid can be doubtful and depends on the language and bidder's guaranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bidder's guaranty is conditioned on acceptance of the bid "as a whole," the guaranty may not become effective unless the entire bid is accepted; bidder may refuse to enter into contract for part only of items bid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of delivery is a material element of bid
rubrics_metrics.description: Time of delivery can be a material element of a contract; modifying the time on award (e.g., extending delivery) may be inconsistent with the specifications and spirit of competitive bidding statutes and could require new advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing material terms like delivery times on award could have altered who would have bid; contracting officers should not modify material elements when awarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bids based on minimum shipments must state minimums; cannot materially amend after opening
rubrics_metrics.description: If prices are based on minimum shipments the amount must be clearly stated in the bid. After opening, eliminating the minimum-shipment provision would be a material change and is not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment were permitted, a contract then made would not be illegal, but amendments post-opening are generally disallowed as material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absent contrary statement, bids assumed severable (accept any or all part)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where bidders were advised that "unless a bidder distinctly states otherwise... it will be assumed that he will accept award of all or any part of the quantity on which he bids," a bidder who names distinct prices for several items and makes no mention of "all or none" may have his bid construed as for the items severally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officer justified in construing such bids as severable unless bidder clearly limited acceptance to entire lot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising for proposals required under section 3709 except in exigency
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3709 R.S. provides purchases and contracts for supplies or services shall be made by advertising for proposals "when the public exigencies do not require the immediate delivery of the article or performance of the service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exigency (public necessity for immediate delivery/performance) may justify immediate contract without advertising; examples include contractor failure at a critical stage risking appropriation loss or severe embarrassment to service. But the exigency standard is narrow — the officer must reasonably determine immediate need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer charged with procurement has discretion to determine exigency
rubrics_metrics.description: Law leaves to the officer charged with making the purchase the discretion to determine whether an emergency exists; heads of staff departments supervise but need not personally determine emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinate officers should not in general dispense with advertising on their own theory of exigency without instructions/orders from proper superior; where doubt exists purchases should be referred to higher authority if circumstances permit delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where doubt exists, refer purchasing decision to higher authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is doubt as to the existence of an emergency the contemplated purchase should be referred to higher authority if delay is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Secretary could have authorized an exigency purchase beforehand he may approve after the fact if, in his judgment, the exigency existed; certification by the purchasing officer that exigency existed supports approval when papers do not negative the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3709 applicability depends on whether transaction is 'in the department' or 'supplies'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether advertising is required sometimes depends on whether the purchase is of 'supplies' "in" a department; purchases not for general departmental use (e.g., cadet clothing paid from cadet pay; monuments under certain acts) may not fall within section 3709.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous usage and the source of appropriation are factors in determining whether a transaction falls under section 3709. Cases hold some items (gray cloth for cadets historically purchased from particular mill) may be continued without contravening law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'personal services' under section 3709
rubrics_metrics.description: "Personal services" are services to be rendered in person by the party or parties who contract to furnish them, whether skilled or not (examples: physicians' services, washerwomen, repairing mattresses, hauling rubbish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services performed at a steam laundry where contractor does not perform work personally are not 'personal services.' Payment by the job does not preclude classification as personal services where the party renders services in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-market purchases under June 12, 1906 act (aggregate ≤ $500)
rubrics_metrics.description: The act permits purchase of supplies and procurement of services in the open market when the aggregate amount required does not exceed $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate includes supplies properly grouped in a single transaction and which would be included in a single advertisement; purchases should not be artificially divided to avoid advertising; purchases exceeding $100 must be promptly reported to Secretary under regulations; purchasing officer has discretion on frequency subject to good administration (e.g., buy monthly quantities if appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-market purchase meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: To purchase 'in open market' is to purchase without advertising and in the manner common among business men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-market authority does not require written contract or advertising when aggregate ≤ $500, subject to reporting and other statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: River and harbor (Aug 11, 1888) statute allows non-advertised contracts in emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The act requires contracts for river and harbor improvements be after sufficient public advertisement, but has been construed to permit non-advertised contracts in cases of emergency and to permit contracts 'by contract or otherwise' as Secretary prescribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice courts/authorities have allowed supplemental or non-advertised arrangements (renting government rails to contractor, making supplemental contract to terminate and pay contractor, purchasing contractor's plant to complete work) in emergencies or under Secretary's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition is 'useless' exception to advertising requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising is not required where competition would be useless or impracticable (examples: rare/difficult-to-obtain maps; unique electric power supply; single provider of special wireless telegraph methods; telegraph instruments that can only be sold back to licensor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where true competition cannot reasonably be secured, advertising may be dispensed with under statute allowing exceptions when competition impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single prior fair advertisement suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, pursuant to section 3709 R.S., advertisement has been once duly made, the law has been complied with; if advertisement is without result, it is not necessary (though permissible) to advertise again or to continue advertising until an acceptable bid is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One proper advertisement can satisfy statutory requirement; additional advertising is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material modification of bid terms disallowed post-opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after bid opening that materially change terms (e.g., removing a stated minimum shipment requirement) are not authorized because they change the substance of the bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material changes could convert the procurement into a de facto contract without competition; if permitted, may render resulting contract legally valid, but generally such post-opening changes are disallowed.
